source: BK3 printed p.41 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.47; Step 7 speculative derivation from topology
note: Speculative (Step 7): every expect is derived by hand from the five wires and the p.41 rule (either pushbutton pushed -> light 3 ON; both pushed -> light 3 not ON). The page prints the either-pushed and both-pushed cases only; the neither-pushed case is derived (C-17) and is checked here at the start and at the end, and the pushbutton-2-only case is checked by releasing pushbutton 1 while 2 is held. Topology: 1+ feeds arm 1Y only; pushbutton 1 steers that feed to 1Z (up, to 2X) or 1X (down, to 2Z); pushbutton 2's arm 2Y picks 2Z (up) or 2X (down) and feeds light 3 (2Y/3A, 3B/3-). Light 3 is lit exactly when the two buttons differ. No relay, switch or motor is used and nothing loops back, so each input set has one settled state. The 500 ms advance before each expect lets the lamp finish its thermal transient; the page states no timing.

script.cite: BK3 printed p.41 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.47, stated rule EITHER BUT NOT BOTH (pushbutton 1 = A, pushbutton 2 = B, light 3 = C; either pushed -> light 3 ON, both pushed -> light 3 NOT ON); ER-10 names it EXCLUSIVE OR; derived from topology: neither pushed (C-17, not printed). 1+/1Y feeds arm 1Y, which rests on 1Z, so 1Z/2X makes 2X live; arm 2Y rests on 2Z, and 2Z is wired only to 1X, which pushbutton 1 (up) leaves dead; 2Y/3A dead, light 3 (3A-3B-3-) dark
script.quote: The program uses the contacts so that if either pushbutton 1 or pushbutton 2 is pushed, light 3 will come ON. Light 3 will NOT come on if both pushbuttons 1 and 2 are pushed.
